subject: chemistry
question_text: In what respect does lithium hydrogen carbonate differ from the other alkali metal hydrogen carbonates?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The difference
lines: It cannot be obtained as a solid.
stable solids and can be isolated.
steps.why: The question asks for a difference, so the answer has to state both sides: what lithium hydrogen carbonate does, and what the other alkali metal hydrogen carbonates do.
common_mistakes: Writing that LiHCO₃ does not exist at all. It exists in solution; it is the solid that cannot be obtained.
Giving the lithium half only. Say plainly that the other alkali metal hydrogen carbonates are solids.
steps.memory_tip: Lithium's hydrogen carbonate exists only in solution; the rest of group 1 give solids.
steps.margin_note: Both sides of the difference must be written.

steps.label: The reason
lines: Li⁺ is the smallest alkali metal ion, so
its charge to size ratio is the highest
It distorts the large HCO₃⁻ ion strongly
and weakens it, so on evaporating the
solution the salt changes to lithium
steps.why: The high charge to size ratio of Li⁺ is what sets lithium apart from the rest of group 1. Here it weakens the large hydrogen carbonate ion so much that the solid salt never forms.
common_mistakes: Writing that Li⁺ carries a bigger charge. Every alkali metal ion is +1; lithium differs by size.
Naming lithium hydroxide as the product. The decomposition gives lithium carbonate, carbon dioxide and water.
steps.memory_tip: The smallest cation distorts the large hydrogen carbonate ion so strongly that no solid salt forms.
steps.margin_note: Name the three products if the equation is written.

insider_note: Magnesium behaves the same way, and this is one item on the lithium and magnesium similarity list: neither forms a solid hydrogen carbonate.
